featuredImage.alt: How to Get Rid of Bed Bug Infested Furniture

c: Discovering bed bugs in your furniture can be stressful. Once you find signs of an infestation in a mattress, sofa, bed frame, recliner, or other upholstered furniture, one of the first questions is usually:
How do I get rid of bed bug infested furniture without spreading the bugs throughout my home or to someone else’s property?
The answer isn’t simply to carry the furniture outside.
Bed bugs are excellent hitchhikers and can move from furniture, bedding, clothing, boxes, and other belongings into new areas.
If you have decided that an infested piece of furniture needs to be removed, it should be handled carefully, sealed properly, and disposed of responsibly.

c: Not necessarily.

According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, furniture should not automatically be discarded if the bed bugs can be safely eliminated. Treatment may sometimes allow furniture to remain in the home.

If you’re unsure whether the furniture can be salvaged, consider consulting a qualified pest management professional before throwing it away.

blocks.text: Don’t Move Infested Furniture Around Your Home

c: One of the biggest mistakes people make is moving an infested couch, mattress, or bed frame from one room to another.
This can spread bed bugs to areas that weren’t previously affected.
Bed bugs can hide in seams, cracks, upholstery, furniture joints, and other small spaces.
If you’re planning to dispose of an infested item, avoid dragging it through multiple rooms unnecessarily.
Plan the removal route before moving anything.

The purpose isn’t to destroy furniture unnecessarily. It’s to prevent someone from unknowingly taking an infested item home.
Don’t assume that you can simply leave an infested sofa or mattress anywhere.
Municipalities have different rules for oversized furniture, mattresses, and pest-infested items.

For example, the City of Toronto allows oversized furniture and mattresses to be collected at the curb, but specifically requires furniture or mattresses infested with bed bugs to be completely wrapped in plastic before collection.
Toronto also requires infested mattresses to be wrapped in plastic for certain drop-off options.
If you live elsewhere in the GTA, check the rules for your municipality before setting an infested item outside.

blocks.text: Don’t Hide the Bed Bug Problem

c: Never tell a removal company that a piece of furniture is “just old” if you know it contains bed bugs.
The infestation needs to be disclosed.
Bed bugs can spread through contact with infested furniture and belongings, so responsible communication helps protect workers, other customers, and the wider community.
Mattresses are one of the most common items people want to dispose of after discovering bed bugs.
Before throwing one away, determine whether it can be treated.
If disposal is necessary:

items: Keep the mattress in the affected area until you’re ready to remove it.
Clearly mark it as bed bug infested.
Follow your municipality’s collection or disposal requirements.
Move it directly to the designated collection point or removal vehicle.

blocks.text: What About Couches and Upholstered Furniture?

c: Sofas, loveseats, recliners, and upholstered chairs can have numerous hiding places.
Bed bugs may hide in:
If the furniture cannot be effectively treated or you have decided to replace it, carefully wrapping and removing it is important.
Don’t leave cushions or pieces separately around the property where someone could pick them up.

blocks.text: Don’t Replace the Furniture Too Quickly

c: Getting rid of an infested mattress or sofa doesn’t mean you should immediately buy a replacement.
If bed bugs are still present in the room, new furniture can become infested too.
Toronto’s guidance specifically notes that replacement items may become infested if brought into an affected room before the infestation has been controlled.
Treat the infestation first, then bring new furniture into the space.

blocks.text: What Should You Do With Other Belongings?

c: Furniture isn’t the only thing that can carry bed bugs.
They can hitchhike on:
The EPA recommends using appropriate treatment and handling methods for potentially infested items rather than simply moving them from one room to another.
For washable clothing and bedding, high-temperature drying can be an important part of bed bug control.
Bed bugs can make people desperate for a quick solution, but some home remedies can create serious risks.

For example, the EPA warns against attempting to heat an entire home using thermostats, propane heaters, fireplaces, or similar methods. These approaches can be dangerous and are not reliable bed bug treatments.
If the infestation is extensive, working with a qualified pest management professional can be a safer approach.

blocks.text: What Happens to the Furniture After Removal?

c: Once an infested item has been safely removed, its final destination depends on the material, condition, and available disposal or processing options.
Some materials may be recoverable, while severely infested upholstered furniture may require disposal.
The priority is preventing the item from being reused or redistributed in a way that could spread bed bugs.
Responsible junk removal isn’t simply about getting an unwanted item out of your house.

b: It’s also about making sure the item doesn’t become someone else’s problem.
